summary: Round 3: hunt NON-OBVIOUS / un-thought-of UK gaps (emerging, second-order, transplant-arbitrage) with adversarial novelty verification

survivors.title: DUAA Article 22A-D AI-hiring safeguard stack (challenge portal + meaningful-human-review evidence log)
survivors.problem: From 5 Feb 2026 the DUAA replaced UK GDPR Art 22 with Arts 22A-22D: solely-automated recruitment decisions are allowed only if four safeguards are operational - notify the candidate, allow representations, give genuine human intervention, and let them contest. There is no off-the-shelf UK product operationalising this: a candidate-facing 'request human review / challenge' intake portal, a tamper-evident log proving the human review was meaningful (not rubber-stamping an AI shortlist), the Art 22 transparency notice, DPIA and vendor-bias-audit evidence pack. Employers bolt this onto an ATS by hand or ignore it.
survivors.who_suffers: UK employers running AI sifting/scoring (HireVue/Eightfold/Greenhouse-style or homegrown LLM CV-scoring), in-house recruitment/RPO teams and HR-tech vendors who must hand clients a compliance wrapper. ~54% of UK SMEs deploy AI; tens of thousands hire at volume.
survivors.merged_evidence: ICO recruitment ADM report (31 Mar 2026) sampled 30+ UK employers, found MOST use AI as ADM without applying safeguards, sent advisory letters to 16 named orgs (privacymatters.dlapiper.com). 'Most UK Employers Using AI Hiring Tools Are Non-Compliant' as ICO consultation closed 29 May 2026 (techtimes.com). ICO finding that human review often = 'scanning an AI shortlist and approving it', which it rejects as meaningful (staffingindustry.com). ICO safeguards blog Mar 2026. Searches found only law-firm explainers and GRC generalists, no purpose-built tool.
survivors.why_novel: Duty is ~4 months old; ICO enforcement signal landed Mar-May 2026. Generalist GRC vendors treat ADM as one DPIA checkbox; ATS vendors punt to the DPO. The US precedent (NYC Local Law 144 bias-audit industry) does NOT map - the UK route is a data-protection safeguards regime, not a bias-audit law, so US audit firms don't fit and nobody built the UK-shaped version. Founder's reflex 'this is just a DPIA' is wrong: it's a candidate-facing challenge/contest workflow plus meaningful-review evidence.
survivors.ai_unlock: LLM auto-drafts the Art 22 notice and DPIA from a few ATS questions, triages incoming candidate challenge requests, surfaces the specific data points that drove a rejection so a human reviewer genuinely engages (defeating the rubber-stamp finding), auto-generates the meaningful-human-involvement audit log, and parses a vendor's model card into the procurement evidence pack.
survivors.monetization: SaaS £99-499/mo by hiring volume for the challenge portal + review-log + auto-DPIA; white-label tier sold to ATS/RPO vendors; one-off 'ADM readiness audit + evidence pack' £1.5-5k wedge.
source_lenses: FRESHEST UK regulation with no tooling

survivors.defensibility: Low. The product is a workflow (candidate intake/ticketing) + tamper-evident review log + document templates (transparency notice, DPIA, bias-audit evidence pack). All buildable by AI in weeks and equally copyable. No data moat, no network effect. Real moats: (1) speed to capture the 4-month-old regulatory window, (2) becoming the white-label safeguards wrapper embedded in HR-tech/RPO vendors before ATS incumbents ship it natively, (3) regulator-credible templates buyers trust. ATS native build-out within 12-18 months is the dominant commoditisation threat; adjacent incumbents (Warden, Holistic, OneTrust) could bolt on the candidate-facing layer but are pointed at enterprise/model-audit, not SME volume hirers.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE - genuinely unbuilt UK-shaped niche with a hard regulatory trigger and live ICO enforcement signal, but thin moat, SME willingness-to-pay risk, and a closing window make it a fast white-label-to-vendors land-grab, not a durable product.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Fast build (weeks via AI: intake portal + hash-chained review log + template pack). Revenue in 3-6 months IF sold as a white-label wrapper to HR-tech/RPO vendors and outsourced recruiters who must hand clients compliance, rather than direct to SMEs (slow, low-ACV, compliance-theatre buyers). Cold outbound to the 16 ICO-named orgs and recruitment agencies is the warmest entry; no network needed, but solo sales grind is the bottleneck to £1m ARR (~1,000 SMEs at £80/mo, or ~30 vendor white-label deals at £30k).

survivors.title: DMCCA agent-conduct recorder: liability evidence + breach-flagging for UK SMEs running customer-facing AI agents
survivors.problem: On 9 Mar 2026 the CMA published binding-in-practice guidance: a UK business is responsible for what its AI agent says/does as for an employee, must continuously monitor outputs/complaints, must not mislead on whether a customer is dealing with AI, and must surface pre-contract info (price, identity, cancellation rights) or it is a DMCCA breach regardless of consumer harm - fines up to 10% of global turnover. Tens of thousands of UK SMEs have bolted a chatbot onto Shopify/WooCommerce but have no structured record of what their agent promised, no flagging when it over-promises a refund or omits cancellation rights, and nothing to produce if challenged.
survivors.who_suffers: UK SMEs running customer-facing AI agents: e-commerce (~340k+ active UK online stores), plus estate agents, brokers, clinics, tradespeople using booking/quote bots. Near-term buyers: tens of thousands of UK SMBs who have already deployed conversational agents.
survivors.merged_evidence: CMA 'Complying with consumer law when using AI agents' (gov.uk, 9 Mar 2026) demands ongoing monitoring of outputs/interactions/complaints and human oversight. Law-firm alerts confirm 10% turnover fines and that omitting required info is a breach regardless of harm (TLT, Taylor Wessing, CMS). Real precedent: Air Canada chatbot liability; prompt-injection '80% discount' attack on an £8,000 order (aardwolfsecurity.com). Every result is a lawyer explaining the rule; none is a product operationalising it for SMEs.
survivors.why_novel: Regulation ~4 months old. Space occupied entirely by law-firm alerts and enterprise AI-governance platforms (Maxim, Lyzr, Tetrate) selling MCP audit logging to engineering teams. Nobody translated the CMA/DMCCA checklist into a lightweight conduct-recorder + breach-alerter for a non-technical UK shopkeeper.
survivors.ai_unlock: An LLM reads each outbound agent message in near-real-time and judges it against the CMA checklist (Did it disclose it's AI? Omit cancellation/price/identity? Promise a refund/discount outside policy? Contradict the merchant's T&Cs?), then logs a tamper-evident evidence record - classification/reasoning impossible to automate cheaply before.
survivors.monetization: SaaS £19-99/mo per SME by agent volume; 'compliance evidence pack' export as a paid add-on; white-label to chatbot vendors and UK agencies who deploy bots and want to offload liability.

existing_solutions.name: EcomIntercept
existing_solutions.note: Closest adjacent. Sub-100ms guardrail API for ecommerce chatbots on Shopify/WooCommerce/Intercom; blocks prompt injection, unauthorized discounts, off-topic. PREVENTS bad inputs but does NOT create a liability audit trail, does NOT flag missing cancellation rights/pre-contract info, does NOT reference CMA/DMCCA. Same buyer, different job. €0/€29/€99/€399 per month.

existing_solutions.name: ComplianceGuard AI (Shopify app)
existing_solutions.note: Automates Google Merchant Center policy audits to prevent store suspensions. Adjacent SMB-compliance pattern proving shopkeepers buy lightweight compliance apps, but scope is ad-policy not AI-agent conduct.

existing_solutions.name: Lorikeet / Fini / Kore.ai
existing_solutions.note: AI support agents WITH built-in audit trails for regulated industries (finance/healthcare). Enterprise-targeted, bundled into the agent itself; not a standalone recorder for a third-party Shopify bot, not UK-DMCCA-framed.
existing_solutions.funded: VC-backed (Lorikeet, Fini both raised seed/Series A)

existing_solutions.name: Maxim AI / Lyzr / Swept AI / MightyBot
existing_solutions.note: Enterprise AI-governance/observability platforms selling agent audit logging, eval and compliance to engineering teams. Wrong altitude and buyer; not a no-config SME conduct-recorder.

existing_solutions.name: Tidio Lyro / Gorgias / Zipchat (incumbent SMB chatbots)
existing_solutions.note: The chatbots SMEs already run. They store transcripts but do not flag DMCCA/CMA breaches or produce structured liability evidence. Each is a platform risk: could bolt this on as a feature.

existing_solutions.name: EU Withdrawal/Cancellation Button Shopify apps
existing_solutions.note: Not a competitor but a strong demand analog: SMEs buy cheap deadline-driven compliance apps (EU right-of-withdrawal, June 2026 Shopify deadline) reactively. Validates willingness-to-pay for regulatory-checkbox tooling.

survivors.defensibility: Weak-to-moderate. No regulatory moat (rules are public), no data moat early, and the core (log transcripts + LLM-flag missing disclosures/over-promises) is a feature any incumbent chatbot (Tidio, Gorgias, Zipchat) or guardrail vendor (EcomIntercept) can add. The only durable edges are: (1) a curated, continuously-updated UK DMCCA/CMA + EU AI Act Art.50 ruleset translated into plain-English merchant checks (a content/maintenance moat, not a tech one); (2) being the named compliance system-of-record SMEs point to if challenged (switching cost once it holds your evidence). Realistically a 12-18 month window before platforms absorb it.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Fast to first revenue (weeks-to-months): coding is free, the build is a transcript ingest + LLM rule-classifier + dashboard/exportable evidence pack, distributable as a Shopify app + JS snippet. But £1m ARR is slow/uncertain because demand is latent until the first UK enforcement action — pre-fine, this is sold as insurance to non-technical shopkeepers with low urgency and high CAC for a no-audience solo founder.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE - genuinely under-served and timely with no direct UK competitor, but it is a feature with weak defensibility, latent (pre-enforcement) demand, and a hard cold-sell to non-technical SMEs for a solo no-network founder; pursue only as a fast, cheap Shopify-app wedge, not a venture bet.

survivors.title: SME cyber-insurance evidence-pack builder: turn 'we have MFA' into the proof underwriters now demand at renewal
survivors.problem: UK cyber-insurance underwriting flipped 2024-26 from tick-box questionnaires to EVIDENCE-based: insurers require screenshots of MFA config, EDR deployment reports, dated backup-restore test logs, patch reports, IR plans and training records at renewal. If answers don't match the technical reality at the time of a breach, the claim is voided (forensic teams compare proposal answers to VPN logs/AD config post-incident). The SME has no clear owner for this - it falls between the outsourced IT provider and the office manager - producing a last-minute scramble each year and a warranty trap where an honest-but-unevidenced answer destroys cover when it's needed.
survivors.who_suffers: UK SMEs buying/renewing cyber insurance; the majority of UK businesses now hold or are quoted cover and renewal is annual. Acute for the long tail without an in-house security function (professional services, small e-commerce, clinics, charities). Hundreds of thousands of UK SME policies renew yearly.
survivors.merged_evidence: 'The cyber insurance market has shifted from questionnaire-based to evidence-based underwriting' (thecoylegroup). 'Assembling evidence falls between IT providers and internal admin with no clear owner, resulting in last-minute scrambles' (procheckup). 82% of denied claims involved orgs without MFA fully implemented; forensic teams compare answers to network reality (theunitegroup). Advice is literally 'build a repeatable proof packet by hand' (seedpodcyber). No SME-side product exists.
survivors.why_novel: Brand-new (2024-26) consequence of a hard insurance market; the obligation crept onto SMEs faster than tooling. Security vendors sell controls (MFA, EDR), not 'prove-it-to-your-insurer' evidence packs. Insurers/brokers happily push the burden down. The cross-cutting nature (identity + endpoint + backup + HR training) means no single product owns it.
survivors.ai_unlock: AI parses the specific proposal form, maps each question to the exact evidence artefact, pulls/normalises exports from Microsoft 365/Entra, Google Workspace, common EDR/backup tools, auto-generates the screenshot-and-report bundle, and red-flags any question the business cannot truthfully evidence BEFORE they sign (avoiding the warranty trap).
survivors.monetization: £20-60/mo SaaS per SME for an always-current evidence vault + annual renewal-pack export; white-label to insurance brokers and MSPs (perfect distribution); one-off £149 renewal-pack generation for non-subscribers.

existing_solutions.note: Automated evidence collection via M365/endpoint integrations, but framed for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA. Vouch partnership embeds a cyber policy and uses SOC2 status as a premium-signal proxy; does NOT map to a specific insurer's proposal form or build a warranty-defence pack. Heavily funded, US-anchored.

existing_solutions.name: Drata
existing_solutions.note: Same model as Vanta. Has a UK Cyber Essentials module that connects tools and collects evidence with no screenshots — closest to the technical engine needed. Aimed at certification, not insurer proposal/warranty.

existing_solutions.name: GetCybr
existing_solutions.note: UK-focused Cyber Essentials automation, lists an 'Insurance Readiness' feature. Closest adjacent threat. Sold to MSPs/vCISOs (multi-client delivery), not SME-direct, and centred on CE certification rather than the insurer's proposal form / dated restore logs / warranty trap.

existing_solutions.name: Cowbell
existing_solutions.note: SMB-focused cyber insurance MGA with continuous external risk scanning (Cowbell Factors). Evidence is tied to buying Cowbell's own policy; not a portable, insurer-agnostic proof pack the SME owns.

existing_solutions.name: Stoik
existing_solutions.note: European (FR/DE/AT) cyber-insurance startup bundling scans + tools with its own policy. Replaces questionnaires with automated tests for ITS OWN underwriting; not a standalone insurer-agnostic evidence product, and not UK-active in this form.

existing_solutions.name: Coalition / At-Bay
existing_solutions.note: Active-insurance carriers doing continuous monitoring of their own policyholders. US-anchored; evidence locked to their policy.

existing_solutions.name: ISMS.online / SecPortal
existing_solutions.note: UK evidence libraries letting you upload screenshots/exports and link to controls — but manual upload, framed for CE/ISO assessor review, not auto-pulled live config mapped to an insurer warranty.

existing_solutions.name: MSP services (Procheckup, The Unite Group, Seedpod, ITSupport-UK)
existing_solutions.note: The actual status quo. UK commentators explicitly advise SMEs to 'build a repeatable proof packet by hand.' Confirms NO SME-side product exists; it is sold as bespoke service or done manually.

survivors.defensibility: Weak. The technical core — OAuth into M365/Defender/backup tool, pull live config, timestamp, snapshot, render to PDF — is exactly what Vanta/Drata/GetCybr already ship. An 'insurance evidence pack' template is a feature-add for an incumbent, not a defensible product. The only durable moat is a proprietary mapping library: every UK underwriter's proposal/warranty question -> the precise evidence artefact that satisfies it, kept current as carriers tighten terms. That is real but slow-built editorial/research IP (the founder's strength), not a tech moat. Distribution moat (broker/MSP channel) is the realistic lock-in but is exactly what a no-network solo founder lacks.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow-to-medium. Sensitive live integrations (granting an unknown solo vendor read access to AD/M365) lengthen the SME trust cycle; a manual/upload MVP can ship in weeks but the auto-pull version that justifies pricing takes longer. Realistic first paid customers via brokers/MSPs, which means relationship selling, 3-6+ months to meaningful revenue.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE — genuinely under-served and a real recurring UK pain, but weak defensibility (incumbent feature-add) plus a low-ACV SME-direct / broker-channel sale that punishes a no-network solo founder. Pursue only if reframed as a broker/MSP-distributed proprietary 'proposal-question -> evidence-artefact' mapping product, not a generic evidence scanner.

survivors.title: Care-funding evidence file: a continuously-built, council-proof record defending self-funders against 'deliberate deprivation of assets'
survivors.problem: When an older person's assets fall and they later need LA care help, councils can allege 'deliberate deprivation of assets' with NO time limit, treating given-away money as notional capital the family must still fund. Families have no contemporaneous, structured record showing WHY money was spent (legitimate living costs, repairs, usual holidays) versus deliberate avoidance. The evidence that would win a challenge - purpose and reasonableness at the time of each transaction - is exactly what no one captures while it's happening. No UK tool builds this defence file as you go.
survivors.who_suffers: Self-funders with assets near the means-test threshold and the adult children/attorneys managing their money. The over-65 self-funding population and the sandwich generation number in the millions; the at-risk-of-a-challenge subset is a meaningful slice given fast-rising care costs.
survivors.merged_evidence: Age UK factsheet (Sept 2025) on deprivation rules and notional-capital treatment. No time limit on lookback / no '7-year rule' (lottie.org, carehome.co.uk). Councils request bank statements and challenge rapid wealth reduction (ms-solicitors); live council policy (Portsmouth ASC). Framework is entirely evidence-and-intent based yet no consumer tool helps assemble the evidence.
survivors.why_novel: Adversarial, future-contingent ('build proof now for a fight that might happen in 5 years') that consumers under-prioritise and nobody is incentivised to sell - councils benefit from the family's lack of records and solicitors only engage once a challenge lands. Distinct from attorney-accounts: the defence-framing (intent/reasonableness narrative, gift logging, threshold-aware alerts) is untouched.
survivors.ai_unlock: AI reads ongoing statements, classifies spending into 'normal/expected' vs 'deprivation risk', prompts the family to attach a contemporaneous reason for large outflows/gifts, models proximity to the means-test threshold, and on demand generates a structured dated dossier framed to the council's own deprivation criteria.
survivors.monetization: Household subscription ~£5-10/mo often bought at a care-needs scare; one-off defence-dossier export; referral channel to community-care solicitors when a challenge is live. Co-product with the attorney-accounts tool (same data, different output).

existing_solutions.name: Plouta
existing_solutions.note: UK financial-wellness app with 'Strategic Gifting' log, digital vault (will twin), net-worth tracking and in-app IHT advisers. Logs gifts but explicitly framed for IHT/7-year-rule, NOT deprivation-of-assets defence. Closest adjacent software; could add intent-framing as a feature. Privately funded/early-stage, no disclosed raise.

existing_solutions.name: Inherrit
existing_solutions.note: Free UK estate-planning app: track assets, designate beneficiaries, log gifts, identify PETs for the 7-year rule, connect to IHT experts. IHT-framed, not care/deprivation-framed.

existing_solutions.name: Sibstar
existing_solutions.note: Debit card + app built specifically for people with dementia and their attorneys; spend limits and real-time notifications. Tracks/controls spend but does NOT capture purpose/intent narrative for a council challenge.

existing_solutions.name: Solicitors / estate planners (Steene Law, MJR, Martin Searle, MP Estate Planning, willsafe.org.uk, careadvocate.co.uk etc.)
existing_solutions.note: Dominant incumbents on the ADVICE side. Sell deprivation-of-assets advice, trusts, asset-protection and reactive challenge representation. None sell proactive consumer record-keeping software; they profit once a challenge lands. This is the real competitive substitute families turn to.

existing_solutions.name: Court of Protection deputy / attorney accounting tools (OPG annual accounts, generic)
existing_solutions.note: Attorneys/deputies must keep accounts; generic spreadsheets and OPG report templates exist. Capture WHAT was spent, not WHY (intent/reasonableness) for a deprivation defence. Distinct, as the brief notes.

survivors.defensibility: Weak-to-moderate. The intent/reasonableness defence-framing is genuinely untouched in consumer software, but there is no real moat: the data model (transactions + purpose notes + threshold alerts + gift log) is trivial for an AI-built competitor, and the two closest adjacencies (Plouta, Inherrit) already log gifts and could bolt on a 'care defence' mode in weeks. No proprietary data, no network effects, no licence barrier. Only durable edge is being first to own the deprivation-of-assets keyword/SEO and a content-led trust brand.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow-to-moderate. Core app is trivial to build (founder's coding is free), but demand is the bottleneck, not supply. This is a future-contingent, low-salience 'insurance against a fight that might never happen' purchase — exactly the category consumers defer. Long, distrustful sales cycle to anxious adult-children/attorneys; no urgent trigger until a council challenge looms (by which point they call a solicitor, not buy software). Realistically 6-12 months to first meaningful recurring revenue, and willingness-to-pay is the key open risk.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE — genuine untouched niche (intent-framed deprivation-of-assets defence file) but the killer is demand, not competition: a future-contingent low-salience purchase with weak moat and easy-to-copy adjacencies. Pursue only as a wedge into a broader care-funding/estate-records product, validated by pre-selling before building.

survivors.title: Bank / fintech account-review response kit: assemble a source-of-funds / KYC-refresh evidence pack on the clock
survivors.problem: When a UK bank or fintech opens an AML review or sends a Request For Information under MLR 2017, the small business gets days to produce a coherent evidence pack: source-of-funds narrative, matching invoices/contracts, ownership structure, transaction explanations, statements showing a paper trail. The account is frequently frozen meanwhile, so cashflow dies. The owner has no template, no idea what 'good' looks like, and assembles a chaotic PDF dump that gets rejected and triggers more questions. The bank's legal KYC/CDD obligation is offloaded wholesale onto the customer under duress.
survivors.who_suffers: UK micro/small businesses and sole traders, especially on fintech banks. Tide reports >650,000 UK business members; Starling, Revolut Business, ANNA add hundreds of thousands. Realistic addressable base: hundreds of thousands of SMEs who will face at least one review, growing as perpetual KYC replaces calendar reviews.
survivors.merged_evidence: Tide freezing accounts 'without notice', reviews 'up to 30 business days', businesses 'in danger of closing after two weeks' (moneynavigator, ukbusinessforums, moneysavingexpert). Financial Ombudsman closure decisions. Perpetual KYC becoming standard 2025-26 (fintech.global). CRITICAL asymmetry: every source-of-funds/AML product (Armalytix, First AML, ComplyAdvantage, FigsFlow) is built for the verifying side - none for the business being interrogated.
survivors.why_novel: The entire AML/KYC software industry is structurally pointed at the institution holding the obligation (who pays for compliance software). The customer being reviewed is the object of compliance, not a buyer, so nobody built a recipient-side tool. Counter-intuitive to build 'help the suspect answer the bank' software, and the pain is episodic (only felt when frozen), so it's invisible to founders who default to selling to compliance teams.
survivors.ai_unlock: An LLM reads the bank's RFI letter, classifies what each question really asks, ingests statements/invoices/contracts, auto-builds a transaction-by-transaction source-of-funds narrative with a tied-out paper trail, flags the transactions likely to trigger follow-ups, and generates a structured professional evidence pack in the format reviewers expect.
survivors.monetization: Urgent one-off 'unfreeze my account' pack £99-399 (cashflow panic = instant pay) + a £15-30/mo 'always-review-ready' subscription keeping a living dossier updated from connected feeds. Affiliate/referral from challenger banks and accountants.

existing_solutions.note: Open-banking source-of-funds analysis, but sold to the VERIFYING side (law firms, financial services, gaming). The reviewed customer only shares data into it; not a recipient-side pack-builder. VC-backed.

existing_solutions.name: First AML
existing_solutions.note: KYC/CDD orchestration for the obligated institution. Institution-side. Funded (Series B).

existing_solutions.name: ComplyAdvantage
existing_solutions.note: AML screening/monitoring for financial institutions. Institution-side. ~$100M+ raised.

existing_solutions.name: SmartSearch
existing_solutions.note: Source-of-funds via open banking sold to regulated firms doing the checking. Institution-side.

existing_solutions.name: Sterling Law / LexLaw / Francis Wilks & Jones / 2 Hare Court
existing_solutions.note: UK solicitors who package source-of-funds/source-of-wealth reports and frozen-account challenges. This is the REAL recipient-side incumbent, but it is bespoke legal services (£££, slow), not a self-serve product. Closest substitute, not a software competitor.

existing_solutions.name: Generic templates (template.net, FINRA small-firm template)
existing_solutions.note: Static fill-in letter templates. No structuring, no evidence assembly, no 'what good looks like'. Free, low quality.

existing_solutions.name: Generic AI doc tools (Fundwriter.ai, Lucid, DataSnipper)
existing_solutions.note: Adjacent AI document/finance tools; none positioned for AML review response. Could be repurposed by a savvy user but nobody markets to this pain.

survivors.defensibility: Weak-to-moderate. The product (template + AI narrative generator + evidence checklist) is trivially cloneable and coding is free. No data moat, no network effect, no integration lock-in (submission is via the bank's own in-app chat, so no API to own). Only durable edges are: a curated, bank-specific playbook library built from real accepted/rejected cases (cold-start, accretes over time) and SEO/brand as the go-to name when someone googles 'Tide account frozen what to do' at the moment of panic. Both are erodible."
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Fast to build (weeks), but slow and lumpy to monetise. Acquisition is the killer: demand is episodic and only exists at the moment of a freeze, so there is no steady-state buyer to retain. Revenue is one-shot, high-intent, panic-driven — closer to a legal-distress funnel than recurring SaaS. First paying customer plausibly within 1-2 months via SEO/Reddit/forum capture; £1m ARR is a long, marketing-heavy climb."
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE — genuine under-served asymmetry (every competitor faces the institution), but it is a one-shot distress purchase, not SaaS; £1m ARR needs huge top-of-funnel and edges toward legal-services territory a solo founder must avoid giving 'advice' in.

survivors.title: Quote-Truth Guard: bind UK SME chatbot/agent promises to a ground-truth price-and-policy ledger before they become legally binding
survivors.problem: UK law (Air Canada precedent, Consumer Rights Act, mistake-price rules) means an SME is generally bound by what its AI agent tells a customer - a hallucinated discount, an invented refund eligibility, a wrong delivery promise, or a price an attacker extracts via prompt injection. SMEs have no guardrail that, at the moment the agent is about to state a price/offer/policy, validates that claim against the business's real current price list, stock and policy ledger and blocks or corrects it before it leaves the bot. Distinct from generic AI safety - it's a narrow transactional truth-check on outbound commercial promises sized for a UK SME's liability surface.
survivors.who_suffers: Any UK SME whose agent quotes prices, discounts, refunds, availability or terms: e-commerce, trades/installers giving quotes, hospitality/clinics taking bookings, B2B suppliers. Tens of thousands already running quote/booking bots.
survivors.merged_evidence: Documented loss: customer talked an AI chatbot into an 80% discount on an £8,000 order via prompt injection (aardwolfsecurity). Air Canada-style precedent + UK liability for chatbot promises (surebright; ABA). UK mistake-price rules force honouring genuine contracts (Citizens Advice). Retailers rewriting T&Cs to dump liability, and UK law making blanket 'AI error' exclusions invalid (slashgear; cms-lawnow).
survivors.why_novel: Prompt-injection-driven commercial promises and resulting UK liability are a 2025-26 phenomenon; current offerings are broad LLM-guardrail/security tools for developers (enterprise) or generic chatbots - none is a narrow 'every price/offer/policy my bot states must match my real ledger or it doesn't ship' product for SMEs. The non-obvious framing is transactional promise integrity tied to UK contract liability, not 'AI security'. Complements the DMCCA conduct-recorder (prevention vs evidencing).
survivors.ai_unlock: An LLM-based outbound interceptor sits between the SME's agent and the customer, extracts any commercial claim (price, %, refund right, delivery date, stock), checks it against a synced ground-truth ledger (the shop's price/policy feed), and blocks/rewrites or routes to human approval if it diverges, logging the prevented event.
survivors.monetization: £15-75/mo per SME by message volume; 'prevented-loss' reporting upsell; bundle with the DMCCA evidencer as one 'agent liability suite'; white-label to UK chatbot vendors.

existing_solutions.name: Galileo Protect / Agent Control
existing_solutions.note: Real-time 'hallucination firewall' intercepting outputs <200ms; can enforce business-rule guardrails and block hallucinations/prompt-injection before reaching users. Free/$100-mo Pro/Enterprise; real-time guardrails gated to Enterprise. Well-funded enterprise/developer category leader. Generic, not SME-packaged, not framed around UK contract liability — but technically does the core mechanism.

existing_solutions.name: Guardrails AI / Guardrails Pro
existing_solutions.note: Open-source validator framework + hosted Pro service for input/output guards (incl. factuality/competitor checks). Developer tool, you compose validators yourself. Not an SME product, no ledger-binding, no UK-liability framing.

existing_solutions.name: ProofSnap ('AI flight recorder')
existing_solutions.note: Records/cryptographically seals what the AI said for court-admissible evidence, explicitly marketed on EU AI Act / UK chatbot-liability / prompt-injection-defence narrative. $8.99/mo. This is the EVIDENCING (post-hoc) complement the gap itself names — already shipping cheaply in the exact legal story the founder would use to sell prevention.

existing_solutions.name: Chaterimo / Chatbase / Alhena / Fin / Tidio (e-commerce chatbots)
existing_solutions.note: Mainstream SME chatbots that already sync live Shopify/store pricing+inventory via API and RAG-ground answers, plus hallucination-detection/QC layers. They claim to keep quotes accurate from source-of-truth, eroding the problem for the largest SME segment (e-commerce) inside the tool SMEs already pay for.

existing_solutions.name: Get BOB (getbob.ai)
existing_solutions.note: NOT a competitor on inspection — a generic AI-automation 'colleague' platform (Texas, $29-499/mo). Surfaced only via a marketing blog post on chatbot guardrails; the product itself does not do transactional truth-checking. Listed to document it was ruled out.

survivors.defensibility: Weak-to-moderate. The core mechanism (ground outbound claim in live price/policy data, block on mismatch) is becoming table-stakes inside the chatbot platforms SMEs already use, and is done at the heavy end by funded enterprise guardrail firewalls. A solo standalone 'truth-check middleware' has no data moat, no network effect, and is squeezed from both sides. The only defensible sliver is deep UK-vertical rule logic (trades/installer quoting, B2B terms) where data is NOT a clean catalog API — but that's a high-touch, narrow wedge, not a horizontal SaaS moat. Integrations into many chatbot stacks is the realistic stickiness, which is exactly what incumbents own.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow-to-medium. The cheap RAG-able segment (e-commerce) is already partly solved by the SME's existing bot, so you must sell against a 'we already do this' incumbent; the genuinely under-served segment (trades/B2B quoting) needs per-vertical rule logic and is a high-touch, non-technical-buyer sale that's hard for a solo no-network founder to scale quickly.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE-leaning-KILL — real legal pain and no exact-fit SME product yet, but the mechanism is commoditising fast (incumbent chatbots already sync live pricing; enterprise firewalls do the heavy version; the evidencing complement, ProofSnap, already ships at $9/mo), leaving a thin, high-touch wedge that's hard for a solo no-network founder to reach £1m ARR on.

survivors.title: Independent-school VAT partial-exemption + Capital Goods Scheme tracker
survivors.problem: From 1 Jan 2025 VAT at 20% applies to UK private school fees, instantly making schools partially exempt (taxable education + still-exempt nursery/welfare) and forcing residual-input-tax apportionment, quarterly provisional recovery, an annual adjustment, and - the killer - Capital Goods Scheme tracking on every building/refurb over £250k and IT over £50k across a rolling 10-year window, plus pre-registration recovery claims. Done today in fragile bespoke Excel by bursars who have never done VAT, with specialist support advised for every claim.
survivors.who_suffers: Bursars/finance directors at ~2,400-2,600 UK independent schools, almost none with an in-house VAT function before 2025. Each is a high-value buyer already paying VAT consultancies (RSM, BDO, PKF, Berthold Bauer) four/five-figure fees per engagement.
survivors.merged_evidence: HMRC guidance confirms partial exemption + CGS apply (gov.uk). RSM: recovery 'more complex for partially exempt businesses, increases likelihood of errors'. PKF Smith Cooper and Berthold Bauer market this as needing specialist help. CGS first adjustments land Sept-Nov 2025 VAT returns (MHA). HMRC confirms partial-exemption calcs are NOT required to sit in MTD software - i.e. MTD vendors deliberately leave it out. Searches found only HMRC manuals, a generic free calculator and consultancy pages.
survivors.why_novel: Pain ~18 months old; VAT vendors treat partial exemption as a manual advisory job explicitly out of MTD scope, so no SaaS targets it. ~2,500 schools is too small for VC-backed platforms, and Big-4/mid-tier earn more from repeated bespoke advisory than from a tool that cannibalises fees.
survivors.ai_unlock: LLM ingests a school's chart of accounts + trial balance + property/IT asset register, classifies supplies as taxable/exempt/residual, runs the standard method + de-minimis + annual adjustment + override test, and generates a defensible CGS schedule with the 10-year math and audit-ready workings, re-explaining the method at HMRC enquiry time.
survivors.monetization: SaaS £1,500-4,000/yr per school (a fraction of one consultancy engagement) plus a 'CGS lifetime register' premium tier (10-year liability tracking = long lock-in). At 300 schools ~£600k-1.2m ARR from a market a VC would dismiss.

existing_solutions.name: Berthold Bauer Consultants (education VAT specialist)
existing_solutions.note: DIRECT THREAT (closest competitor). Education-VAT specialist that already provides schools with 'basic or more bespoke Partial Exemption templates so that Schools can compile VAT returns without relying on third parties.' This is the exact buyer and exact pain, delivered as a productised template + advice-line bundle. They give the self-serve artefact away as part of advisory relationships, undercutting a paid standalone SaaS.

existing_solutions.name: Tax Systems (AlphaVAT / Alphatax)
existing_solutions.note: Enterprise VAT software that ALREADY handles standard AND special-method partial exemption, period comparison, and group VAT. Built for corporates/large orgs, not priced or marketed to schools, but a credible 'move down-market' threat and proves partial-exemption automation is a solved problem technically.

existing_solutions.name: VT Software (VT Transaction+)
existing_solutions.note: Low-cost UK accounting/MTD software with a built-in partial exemption feature. Cheap and widely used by small finance teams. Does not do CGS 10-year tracking or school-specific apportionment, but already covers the headline 'partial exemption calc' that a school tool would lead with.

existing_solutions.name: UKCalculator / WeCovr free VAT partial-exemption & school-fee calculators
existing_solutions.note: Free single-period partial exemption calculators and school-fee VAT estimators. Commodity, no CGS, no annual adjustment, no record-keeping — but they anchor buyer expectation that 'a calculator should be free.'

existing_solutions.name: WCBS HUB / iSAMS / IRIS-Engage school finance MIS
existing_solutions.note: Incumbent school finance/MIS platforms used by most independent schools. Today they handle VAT on outgoing invoices/MTD submission but NOT partial-exemption apportionment or CGS. Highest long-term displacement risk: any of them could add a module and reach all 2,500 schools through an existing contract instantly.
existing_solutions.funded: WCBS/iSAMS PE-backed; IRIS owned by Leonard Green (PE)

existing_solutions.name: Big-4 / mid-tier consultancies (RSM, BDO, PKF Smith Cooper, Crowe, HaysMac, Saffery, Menzies, VAT Solutions)
existing_solutions.note: Sell repeated bespoke advisory: special-method design, CGS first-adjustment reviews, pre-registration claims, and the lucrative Feb-2026 pre-registration tribunal recovery opportunity. They own the buyer relationship and earn far more from advice than a tool would; they are simultaneously a channel and a competitor for trust.

survivors.defensibility: Weak-to-moderate. The domain logic (apportionment + 10-year CGS register + annual adjustment) is genuinely fiddly and would take a competitor real effort to encode correctly — that's a small moat. But there is no data network effect, no switching cost beyond an annual workflow, and the calc engine already exists in enterprise tools (Tax Systems, VT). The fatal exposure is distribution: incumbent school MIS vendors (WCBS/iSAMS/IRIS) can bolt this on and reach all 2,500 schools through existing contracts, and education-VAT consultancies already hand out self-serve partial-exemption templates. A solo founder's only durable edge is being radically cheaper, school-specific, and faster-to-onboard than both — a positioning moat, not a technical one.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow-to-medium. Build is fast (well-defined calc logic, AI-codeable in weeks). But revenue is gated by trust and cadence: a bursar will not run a £20k VAT return through an unknown teenager's tool without proof, and the buying/usage cycle is quarterly/annual, not daily — so sales cycles are long and pilots span a full VAT year. Expect 9-15 months to first meaningful ARR even if the product nails the spec.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE — real, recent, well-defined pain with high-value buyers and no exact-fit SaaS, but a tiny shrinking TAM (~2,500 schools), free/cheap adjacent tools, advisory incumbents who own trust, and MIS vendors who can crush it on distribution; £1m ARR is a genuine stretch for a no-network solo founder.

survivors.title: UK dual-use self-classification + SPIRE licence-decision copilot for hardware/software micro-exporters
survivors.problem: Small UK dual-use makers (drone, RF, sensor, comms, crypto, ML/compute, additive-manufacturing) must self-classify products against the UK Strategic Export Control Lists, choose the right route (no licence / OGEL register on SPIRE / SIEL application), and run an Internal Compliance Programme. Self-classifying one tricky item (encryption, sensors, autonomy) takes an experienced officer hours-to-days; small firms have no such officer and the cost of getting it wrong is criminal liability. Volume is rising as the SME defence push pulls more tech firms into export and SaaS/software-as-export rules catch software shops who don't realise they're exporters.
survivors.who_suffers: UK micro/small dual-use manufacturers and software/SaaS firms exporting controlled tech - drone, electronics, RF, optics, advanced-materials, quantum/compute, crypto startups, plus university spinouts under Trusted Research/ATAS pressure. Thousands of firms; the long tail has no in-house export-control officer.
survivors.merged_evidence: ECJU administers UK military + dual-use controls; ICP expected (gov.uk ECJU, UK strategic export controls). Self-classification 30-60 min simple, days for encryption/sensors and 'more expensive per item than people realise' (peacocktariffconsulting, ec-compliance). SaaS/software-as-export catches unwitting firms (fgx.com). Trusted Research/ATAS/NSI pressure (npsa.gov.uk). Existing software (ec-compliance, MIC, AEB, clearBorder) is enterprise/customs-team, EU/US-EAR-centric; the gov Control List search is a clunky keyword lookup.
survivors.why_novel: Existing classification software is priced for large trade-compliance departments and is EU/US-centric; the UK gov tool is not a guided self-classification with an audit trail. Nobody has built an affordable, UK-list-native, AI-guided self-classify + route-to-SPIRE-decision + ICP-in-a-box for the under-10-FTE dual-use founder. Reads as 'solved' but only for big exporters.
survivors.ai_unlock: An LLM walks a founder through their product's technical parameters, matches against the public UK Control List entries, returns a defensible draft classification with the reasoning/audit trail an ECJU audit demands, tells them whether they need no licence / OGEL / SIEL, and auto-drafts the ICP document.
survivors.monetization: Freemium classifier (one free item) -> £49-199/mo for ongoing classification, OGEL annual-report reminders, ICP maintenance and audit-trail export. Upsell SIEL application drafting.

existing_solutions.name: Lenzo.ai
existing_solutions.note: NEAR-EXACT COMPETITOR. AI export-compliance platform explicitly for SMB exporters with <5 compliance staff. Does classification + licence-route decisions (SIEL/OGEL/no-licence), immutable timestamped audit trail, daily regulatory updates with version-binding, ICP-style workflow. Flat $99-$899/mo - same pricing slot the gap targets. Currently US-CCL/EAR core (15 CFR) + 50+ sanctions lists incl UK Sanctions List, but already publishes UK ECJU/SPIRE SEO blog content - UK self-classification is an obvious roadmap item, not a moat. Funded (Capterra/GetApp listed, active marketing).
existing_solutions.funded: Yes - commercial SaaS, paid acquisition, third-party review listings

existing_solutions.name: ECCN.help
existing_solutions.note: AI-native classifier 'built for trade compliance pros to classify dual-use goods without a consulting invoice or enterprise contract.' Free during beta. US CCL/EAR + ITAR + OFAC only today, but the exact AI-self-classification UX the gap proposes; UK lists are a trivial extension.
existing_solutions.funded: Unknown - free beta, no credit card

existing_solutions.name: TariffWolf
existing_solutions.note: Free AI ECCN classification tool (2026). US-centric. Another cheap/free AI entrant compressing the price of classification.

existing_solutions.name: ec-compliance
existing_solutions.note: AI classification software that explicitly covers 'EU or UK military and dual-use regulations' plus US EAR. Semantic AI suggestion of classifications. Enterprise-leaning, no public SME pricing - but UK lists already in scope.

existing_solutions.name: KYG Trade
existing_solutions.note: AI-powered export classification across US CCL + EU HS dual-use concordance + other country dual-use lists. Multi-jurisdiction, expanding.

existing_solutions.name: Trademo
existing_solutions.note: AI Export Control & Dual-Use Classification Engine. Multi-jurisdiction, mid-market/enterprise. (Site returned 503 on fetch but clearly an active AI dual-use classification product.)

existing_solutions.name: ICP365 / ECG International
existing_solutions.note: Online Internal Compliance Platform pitched explicitly at smaller orgs without sophisticated compliance systems - 'first aid with compliance, no investment.' The 'ICP-in-a-box' component the gap claims is unbuilt is already a product.

existing_solutions.name: clearBorder
existing_solutions.note: UK strategic-trade consultancy + training (not software). Owns UK-buyer relationships and ranks for UK ECCN/SPIRE/OGEL search terms. Human-led; the trusted-name route SMEs prefer for criminal-liability decisions.

existing_solutions.name: ONESOURCE Global Classification (Thomson Reuters) / MIC
existing_solutions.note: Enterprise AI HS+ECCN classification incl UK lists. Priced for large trade-compliance teams - leaves the SME tail open, but signals the function is fully solved at the top.

existing_solutions.name: UK ECJU Control List Classification / Goods Checker / OGEL Checker (gov.uk SPIRE)
existing_solutions.note: Free official tools. Clunky keyword lookup, max 4 items per advisory enquiry, advisory service historically suspended/backlogged. Govt explicitly tells exporters to self-rate as 'the quicker option' - confirms the pain but is the free default any product must beat.

survivors.defensibility: Weak for this founder. The wedge (UK-list-native guided self-rating + real SPIRE-route workflow + ICP, vs sanctions-led tools) is genuinely thinner-served than it looks, but it is the obvious next sprint for Lenzo (already SMB-priced, already does route decisions + audit trail, already writing UK SEO) and for ec-compliance (already 'UK dual-use' in scope). No data moat - the UK control lists are public; classification logic is replicable by any AI. The real moat in this domain is trust/credibility under criminal liability, which a 19-yo solo no-name founder cannot supply - buyers facing 10-year prison exposure want a named expert/consultancy behind a determination, not an anonymous AI, and 'the AI said so' is no legal defence, so the product can't actually de-risk the buyer. That liability dynamic structurally favours consultancies (clearBorder) and funded teams, and punishes exactly this founder profile.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow. Regulated, liability-heavy domain: long trust-building cycle, SMEs buy cautiously, sales likely founder-led and high-touch. AI build is free but credibility is not, and the founder has no network/credentials to shortcut it. Realistically 12-18+ months to meaningful ARR, against a funded incumbent already in the slot.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE-leaning-KILL: real rising UK pain, but Lenzo is a funded near-exact SMB competitor one sprint from the UK wedge, the ICP/audit-trail pieces already exist, and the criminal-liability trust barrier specifically defeats a solo no-credential founder.

survivors.title: Estate-property obligations clock: council-tax windows, empty-homes premiums, unoccupied-insurance lapses on a probate/care-transition home
survivors.problem: When an owner dies or moves permanently into care, the now-empty home enters a maze of time-boxed, recently-changed obligations that penalise delay: council-tax exemption only until probate then a further 6 months, after which the strengthened (2024/2025) empty-homes premium of up to 100%+ bites; standard buildings/contents insurance lapses after ~30-60 days unoccupied so an unendorsed empty-property policy voids claims; utilities keep charging standing charges. Executors and attorneys miss these clocks and get hit with backdated premiums, voided insurance or fraud exposure. No tool watches these per-council, date-driven rules for an estate/care property.
survivors.who_suffers: Executors/administrators of estates with property and attorneys/deputies who moved a donor into care leaving an empty home. ~280k+ deaths/year in England & Wales involve property, plus care-home admissions; the empty-home-during-probate cohort is hundreds of thousands annually.
survivors.merged_evidence: 2025 council-tax rules: exempt until probate then 6 months; empty-homes premium tightened from 2 years to 1 (April 2024) and second-home/empty premiums up to 100% from April 2025 (gov.uk). Hidden empty-home costs incl. insurance (puremagazine). Care-home empty-property conditions (Commons Library). Each billing authority sets its own premiums/exceptions (Harrow, Stockport) - per-council complexity no consumer tracks.
survivors.why_novel: Brand-new penalty regime (premiums tightened 2024-25) so tooling hasn't caught up; sits in the seam between probate admin, insurance and local-government billing so no incumbent owns it. Reads as 'just remember some dates', hiding how council-specific and financially material the misses are.
survivors.ai_unlock: AI ingests date of death/care-admission and postcode, looks up that billing authority's specific exemption/premium policy, builds a personalised obligations timeline, alerts before each cliff edge, drafts the per-council exemption/exception letters, and tells the executor which empty-property insurance endorsement they now legally need.
survivors.monetization: One-off per-estate fee ~£49-99 bundled into a DIY-probate journey, or affiliate/referral on the empty-property insurance the tool surfaces as a time-critical need. White-label to will-writers, probate-sale estate agents and care-funding advisers.

existing_solutions.name: EstateExec
existing_solutions.note: Leading executor task/deadline software but US/Canada only ('state-specific', 'North America'). No UK council tax, empty-homes premium, or UK unoccupied-insurance tracking. Adjacent, not competing.

existing_solutions.name: Exizent
existing_solutions.note: UK B2B estate-administration platform sold to solicitor/legal firms. Focused on case workflow, asset discovery, probate filings - not consumer per-council property-penalty clocks.

existing_solutions.name: Kinherit
existing_solutions.note: UK estate planning + professional executor + probate property insurance partner services. Covers insuring property in probate but as a service/referral, not a date-driven obligations tracker.

existing_solutions.name: Settld
existing_solutions.note: UK bereavement notification service (free) - bulk account closures across 1200+ providers, date-of-death balances. Explicitly does NOT track time-boxed council-tax windows, empty-home premiums or insurance-lapse clocks.

existing_solutions.name: Life Ledger
existing_solutions.note: UK death-notification service (£19). Notifies 1000+ companies incl. councils/insurers but is a one-shot notifier, not an ongoing per-council premium/insurance-lapse monitor.

existing_solutions.name: Everywhen / Insuristic / Homeprotect probate insurance
existing_solutions.note: Probate/unoccupied property insurers. Send their OWN policy renewal reminders and solve the insurance-lapse piece for their customers - but only their policy, no council-tax/premium clock, no neutral cross-obligation tracker.

existing_solutions.name: Estateably / NextChapter / Executor.org
existing_solutions.note: Estate/probate admin software (mostly North America B2B/consumer) with jurisdiction-aware deadline engines, but encode US statutory deadlines, not UK council-specific empty-home premiums or insurance lapse.

survivors.defensibility: Weak. The asset would be a per-council rules table (300+ billing authorities' premiums/exceptions) plus a date-math reminder engine - genuinely tedious to compile but trivially copyable once the value is visible, and AI makes scraping/maintaining council pages cheap for any follower. Crucially, probate-grant status is NOT recorded in any council data feed, so the tool can never auto-detect - it depends entirely on user-entered dates, which means it is fundamentally 'a reminder app with a lookup table'. No data network effect, no proprietary integration, no lock-in. Insurers already own the highest-stakes reminder (lapse) for their own customers.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow. The buyer (a bereaved executor or care-transition attorney) faces this once, has low intent to pay proactively for a niche SaaS, and is a sensitive, expensive-to-reach, zero-repeat audience for a solo founder with no audience/network. Building the per-council ruleset is fast with AI, but acquiring paying users is the bottleneck and there is no organic/viral loop. Realistic monetisation (insurer/solicitor referral) is affiliate-flavoured - against the founder's hard constraints - and the rest is a sub-£50 one-off consumer fee.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE (leaning KILL) - genuinely novel under-served seam and no direct UK competitor, but it reads as a feature, not a company: one-off non-repeat bereaved buyers, no defensibility, no viral loop, and no credible solo-no-network path to £1m ARR. Only viable repositioned as a B2B widget/lead-gen for probate solicitors or unoccupied-property insurers - which collides with the no-network and no-affiliate constraints.

survivors.title: Instrument decontamination / sterilisation-cycle traceability for newly-regulated aesthetics, podiatry, tattoo & piercing clinics
survivors.problem: UK dental practices have mature decontamination compliance tooling driven by HTM 01-05 (per-cycle steriliser logs, instrument-set tracking to the patient record, validation records, 2-year retention). The adjacent clinical-but-non-dental world - podiatry, aesthetics, tattoo/piercing, acupuncture - is held to the SAME standards (podiatry explicitly follows HTM 01-05; aesthetics being pulled into CQC scope and a new local-authority licensing regime confirmed Aug 2025) yet still records autoclave cycles on fading thermal printouts and patient-note scribbles. No digital sterilisation-traceability product is built for these settings.
survivors.who_suffers: UK podiatry/chiropody clinics, the fast-growing non-surgical aesthetics sector (botox/filler clinics now facing licensing), tattoo & piercing studios, acupuncturists - all running reusable instruments through autoclaves with statutory cycle-logging duties. Tens of thousands of premises; aesthetics alone in the tens of thousands and newly compliance-anxious.
survivors.merged_evidence: Podiatry/aesthetics held to HTM 01-05 / CQC infection-control (Prestige Medical standards; Excel Healthcare chiropody autoclave guide citing HTM 01-05 + 2-year retention; footcheck). New aesthetics licensing regime (three-tier Red/Amber/Green, Aug 2025 govt response, detail consultation 2026) demanding patient records/consent/incident evidence (gov.uk; Browne Jacobson). Records still on printouts/data-loggers (CQC dental mythbuster 12).
survivors.why_novel: Decontamination-software vendors are wedded to the NHS dental supply chain and HTM 01-05's dental framing and never sell sideways. Aesthetics/podiatry software (Calyx, Meridiq, Consentz) focuses on bookings/consent/records, not the autoclave audit trail. The aesthetics infection-control duty is only now biting because of the 2025-26 licensing wave, so the pain is freshly created.
survivors.ai_unlock: AI reads autoclave printouts/data-logger exports (photo or file), validates each cycle against time/temp/pressure parameters, auto-links an instrument set/cycle number to the patient appointment, flags failed/out-of-spec cycles, and assembles inspection-ready traceability and validation packs.
survivors.monetization: £20-50/mo per clinic; bundle autoclave-log + per-patient traceability + licence-evidence pack. The 2026 aesthetics licensing consultation and CQC scope creep are the buying triggers; sell through aesthetics training academies and podiatry associations.

existing_solutions.name: Reprolog
existing_solutions.note: Direct competitor. Cloud sterilisation/reprocessing software: per-cycle logging, instrument-set tracking via QR/RFID, compliance docs. Currently dental-framed and US-operated but product is generic decontamination traceability and explicitly markets itself as adaptable to clinic needs — a sideways pivot into podiatry/aesthetics/tattoo is trivial. Undermines the gap's core 'no product exists / vendors never sell sideways' premise.

existing_solutions.name: Agilio iComply
existing_solutions.note: Dominant UK dental compliance platform. Sells steriliser + decontamination-room compliance logbooks (subscription), CQC task management. Logbooks are digitised record-SHEETS, not true per-cycle autoclave-to-patient traceability — but Agilio owns the UK clinical compliance buyer relationship and could extend into adjacent sectors at will.

existing_solutions.name: Consentz
existing_solutions.note: UK aesthetic-clinic software explicitly marketing CQC compliance + product/batch traceability, riding the 2025-26 licensing wave. Owns the aesthetics buyer and the compliance narrative the gap relies on. Does not do autoclave-cycle logging, but most aesthetics use single-use needles so reusable-instrument autoclave burden is low.

existing_solutions.name: Meridiq
existing_solutions.note: All-in-one UK aesthetic clinic software with CQC-ready records and batch/injectable traceability. Same incumbency over the aesthetics buyer; capturing the infection-control compliance spend.

existing_solutions.name: Pabau / Aesthetics Comply
existing_solutions.note: Pabau (aesthetic PM with CQC features) and Aesthetics Comply (CQC registration + compliance checklists/audit tools/score) both sell to aesthetics on regulatory anxiety. Adjacent incumbents that would bundle any decon-log need.
existing_solutions.funded: Pabau: VC-backed (Octopus Ventures); Aesthetics Comply: private

existing_solutions.name: Getinge T-DOC / Censis CensiTrac / Trisoft SSDman / Athera Fingerprint
existing_solutions.note: Enterprise CSSD/hospital instrument-tracking suites (TrayTrac/InstrumenTrac modules, RFID). Prove the category exists but are priced/scoped for trusts, irrelevant to micro-clinics — yet show the software pattern is well-trodden.
existing_solutions.funded: Getinge (public, NASDAQ Stockholm); Censis (acquired by Fortive); Trisoft/Athera private UK

existing_solutions.name: Podiatry PM software (Smilenotes, TM3, PracticePal, Cliniko)
existing_solutions.note: UK podiatry practice-management tools. Genuinely do NOT track autoclave cycles — confirms a real white space in podiatry specifically. But they own the workflow and could add a module; podiatrists are tiny-budget buyers.

existing_solutions.name: Built-in autoclave logging + council paper templates
existing_solutions.note: NOT software vendors but the real status-quo competitor. Modern autoclaves (Enbio, MDS, Amara) ship with printer/USB/SD/Wi-Fi cycle logging; gov.uk + councils supply free template record sheets; digital is 'advisable, not a legal requirement'. The 'good enough free incumbent' that kills willingness-to-pay.

survivors.defensibility: Low. The product (cloud cycle log + QR/RFID instrument-set-to-patient traceability) is technically commoditised — Reprolog already built it for dental and markets it as adaptable, and any aesthetics/podiatry PM incumbent (Consentz, Meridiq, Agilio) can bolt on a decon module within their existing buyer relationship. No data moat, no network effect, no regulatory lock-in for a newcomer. A solo founder's only edge would be sector-specific compliance framing and onboarding, which is copyable.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE leaning KILL — the exact non-dental per-cycle-traceability niche is lightly served, but Reprolog is an adaptable direct product, UK incumbents own each buyer, autoclaves self-log for free, digital isn't legally mandated, and the buyers are fragmented near-zero-budget micro-businesses, making £1m ARR very hard for a solo no-network founder.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow. No legal mandate forcing digital adoption (records are required; the FORMAT is not — paper/printout is explicitly accepted), so demand is discretionary.
